The route whose stages ARE the full-team R/E/R cycle: research → evaluation → recommendation precede any build unit; every stage carries every seat; the public stakes carried at the gates — "so right as we will be talking about this project publicly and this teams work on it" (Q-auth-widening ruling 3).

## THE STAGES (5) — the cycle itself

**evaluation** — THE FULL BENCH OVER THE CANDIDATES (the full-team input mandate: every seat pricing the candidates against its own discipline).
- entry_condition: G-AUTH-RESEARCH is green — the sources read, the claims extracted, the candidates mapped, every seat's input visible.

**recommendation** — THE REASONING WHOLE (the R/E/R mandate: suisen's form at full depth, the collaborator ruling on evidence).
- entry_condition: the evaluation's packets landed whole — every candidate attacked, walked, priced, diagnosed; the divergences carried whole.
- purpose: suisen's full-depth recommendation (ungated) carrying the whole bench's findings — the reasoning whole, the alternatives named with their prices; togo's gated synthesis integrating — the divergences reconciled at the synthesis; THE COLLABORATOR'S RULING on the full record at G-AUTH-DESIGN — the design gate, the public face: the reasoning visible in the record, every choice citable to its seat's own evidence; the build set ruled by the cycle's outcome.

- purpose: the likely set named not pinned — the key infrastructure (mint/verify/rotate/revoke), the policy layer (the grants per identity: who may register, vote, read state, tally), the serving-tier integration (the FastAPI service :8000, the web's session surfaces), the MCP tier's verified-token form (OunceMCP's identity + policies) — THE CYCLE'S OUTCOME RULES THE SET; the two-lane brief→spec→build per unit (G-<UNIT>-BRIEF → G-<UNITSPEC>-BRIEF → G-<UNIT>, minted at their turns); the per-step dispatch (R8, the file-unit); jikko builds one file per dispatch; kensho verifies independently per build gate; MOHO'S IMPLEMENTATION WALKS at the agent/user-facing units' build gates (R4); the seat-authored reports (R6/R11); one-commit-per-increment; the authn+authz scope held (both halves, one design); the llm-class constraint held (the llm's own key, no human-approval gate anywhere); the configurability law at every knob from birth (the key store's home, the header names, the policy toggles); the floor held (203+, pyright 0/0, ruff zero findings, zero ignores); the free-tier spirit (the design prices its own infrastructure).

**close** — THE EFFORT'S BOOKEND (the standing form).
- entry_condition: the route's build gates closed green and the collaborator has called the close.
- purpose: hansei's retro (the friction ledger the intake), the effort's records (the CONTINUATION entry; the next era named — the order-bias probe the inward lane's next, outward after inward, per the CI effort's direction ruling), the done call at the collaborator's ruling.

## THE GATES (the earned trio: collaborator-ruling at the ruling points, deterministic-check at the build gates, assessment at the close's steps)

1. the composition lands at the store's reports home (reports/compose/route.md — keikaku's own report, the composition whole: stages, gates, increments, the ungated placements, the load-bearing decisions) — the opening whole, the R/E/R stages placed BEFORE any build unit, the research placed FIRST with none of its findings assumed, every seat placed (the full-team input mandate: no seat bypassed);

THE SOURCES READ: all four source classes researched whole — OunceMCP's verified-token docs through the claims lane (extract → research → verify → rule, each claim its own verdict: confirmed | refuted | priced-and-accepted | cured), the FastAPI/FastMCP auth ecosystems, the API-key infrastructure landscape (form, storage, rotation, verification, revocation), the threat-model literature;

4. EVERY SEAT'S INPUT VISIBLE: tansa's census, shindan's threat-model diagnosis, rikai's mechanism maps, keisan's landscape arithmetic, moho's exposure walk — the full-team record IS the public face; a divergence that survives reconciliation blocks the gate, never rides silently;

**G-AUTH-DESIGN** (collaborator-ruling) — the design gate, the cycle's ruling (THE COLLABORATOR'S RULING on the full record):

3. THE REASONING VISIBLE: the record carries the cycle's whole reasoning — the public face, every choice citable to its seat's own evidence;
4. THE BUILD SET RULED + THE SCOPE HELD: the collaborator's ruling names the build units (the cycle's outcome rules the set); the authn+authz scope held (both halves, one design — the key without the policy is a door with no rooms); the llm-class constraint carried across both halves (the llm's own key, no human-approval gate anywhere); the configurability law at every knob from birth;
5. no build dispatch fires before it is green.

**G-<UNIT>-BRIEF / G-<UNITSPEC>-BRIEF** (collaborator-ruling, minted per unit at its turn) — the two-lane standing shape: the brief (togo's synthesis over the unit's ungated discovery legs discover/<unit> + understand/<unit> + the approved design — the banked shapes, the scope fence, the return forms) and the spec (the bytes whole, every edit fenced-bytes-exact, the per-file dispatch plan R8); the dispatches cite the approved brief/spec; the collaborator approves each — the fires come only after.

**G-CLOSE** (collaborator-ruling) — the standing bookend: hansei's retro landed (the friction ledger the intake, the lessons named); the effort's records landed (the CONTINUATION entry, the landing state named honestly; the next era named — the order-bias probe next on the inward lane, outward after inward); the collaborator rules the close — the done call recorded same-turn, the route's status set done at the ruling.

[steps: build (semantic, jikko, gate) + floor-green (deterministic, make, gate)]

## THE UNGATED PLACEMENTS (the parallel packets — each seat its own discipline; the evidence landing as packet results with evidence files under the store's evidence home .junro/evidence/Q-auth-design/)

- research/census — tansa: the discovery census over the four source classes (OunceMCP's verified-token docs via the claims lane; the FastAPI/FastMCP auth ecosystems; the API-key landscape: form/storage/rotation/verification/revocation; the threat-model literature)

- evaluation/walks — moho: the blind walks of the candidate surfaces
- evaluation/pricing — keisan: the pricing of every candidate against the four constraints
- evaluation/exposure — shindan: the exposure diagnosis of every candidate

- recommendation/auth — suisen: the full-depth recommendation carrying the whole bench's findings (the reasoning whole, the alternatives named with their prices)

- BEARER: FastAPI's APIKeyHeader declares the header once; the route's dependency resolves it at the door before the handler body. - CONSTANT-TIME: hmac.compare_digest runs in time ∝ input length, never ∝ match length — a naive == short-circuits at the first differing byte, leaking the key's prefix through response timing (the timing oracle); compare_digest closes it.
- HASHED-AT-REST: the store holds the digest (sha/blake over the key), plaintext never on disk; the lookup hashes the presented key and seeks the digest (a fixed-length-digest dict lookup — constant per key), the record {digest, comparator_id, scopes, created_at} one self-describing line (the JSONL school, run_store.py:111-120).

# Auth-source census — tansa, 2026-11-24

## 1. OunceMCP verified-token model (subbusainath.github.io/ouncemcp/concepts/security/, /guides/safe-writes/)

- Token's form → identity: `ctx.identity` comes only from the verified access token — principal (issuer+subject), tenant, scopes, claims; `clientInfo` is never used (SEC-1).
- Hide-and-refuse: `policy=` on the server and per tool; one decision hides the tool from lists and search AND refuses calls (SEC-2); policies read the effect declared at registration, never MCP annotations (SEC-3).
- Audience scoping: `OunceServer(audience=...)` checks `aud`/`resource`; `check_outbound` and `passthrough_guard()` block forwarding the caller's token (SEC-4); caches keyed by principal/tenant/scopes (SEC-5).
- Caller-bound handles: `ctx.issue_state`/`ctx.verify_state` bind tokens to caller+request+expiry, `consume=True` single-use (SEC-6); replay-safe effects (SEC-7); `safe_client` refuses private/loopback/link-local/metadata addresses and re-checks every redirect (SEC-9); auth = FastMCP providers, OunceOAuth client (SEC-10).
- stdio: FastMCP skips component authorization over stdio (server runs as the local user); default `stdio_policy="trust"` makes every tool visible/callable; `"enforce"` applies every check with the anonymous caller; `ouncemcp check` warns (stdio-skips-policy).
- Writes: `approval="required"`/function + `preview=`; the model cannot approve by itself; `idempotency=True` keys by caller+tenant+arguments (RedisStore for replicas).
- Verified against the 2026-11-22 census (.plans/ideation/2026-11-22-prioritree-mcp/reports/census/ouncemcp.md): consistent — handles/approval (pt 3), signed cursors + redacted traces (pts 2/5), FastMCP 4.1.6 substrate (pt 4). New detail here: identity shape, clientInfo exclusion, audience/passthrough_guard, stdio_policy, safe_client. No contradictions.

## 2. FastAPI/FastMCP/Starlette ecosystems

- FastAPI (fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/security/, /tutorial/security/first-steps/, /tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt/, /reference/security, /advanced/security/): OpenAPI schemes apiKey (query/header/cookie), http bearer, oauth2 flows (implicit/clientCredentials/authorizationCode/password), openIdConnect; fastapi.security utilities inherit SecurityBase → automatic OpenAPI/docs integration; OAuth2PasswordBearer extracts the Bearer token as a str, 401 on missing header; APIKeyHeader/APIKeyQuery/APIKeyCookie extract the key from header/query/cookie; JWT tutorial: HS256 with an openssl-generated secret, sub/exp claims, dummy-hash verify to equalize timing.
- FastMCP (gofastmcp.com/servers/auth, /servers/auth/token-verification): "Authentication applies only to FastMCP's HTTP-based transports"; "The STDIO transport inherits security from its local execution environment"; default auth=None (unauthenticated; gateway enforcement is the deployer's responsibility). Provider spectrum: TokenVerifier (base; JWTVerifier: jwks_uri+issuer+audience, RS*/PS*/ES*/Ed25519/Ed448, HS via the public_key param; JWKS auto-rotation), RemoteAuthProvider (DCR), OAuthProxy (non-DCR: GitHub/Google/Azure/AWS), OAuthProvider (full authorization server), MultiAuth (first successful verification wins). Opaque tokens via RFC 7662 introspection; each session is bound to the credential that created it (different credential on an Mcp-Session-Id → 404); session identity = (client_id, issuer, subject).
- Starlette (starlette.dev/authentication/, /middleware/): AuthenticationMiddleware + AuthenticationBackend.authenticate(conn) → request.user (BaseUser: is_authenticated/display_name; SimpleUser/UnauthenticatedUser) + request.auth (AuthCredentials.scopes); @requires scope decorator (403, or 404 "to hide information about the URL layout"); middleware forms: pure-ASGI (scope/receive/send), BaseHTTPMiddleware (dispatch(request, call_next); contextvars limitation), built-ins CORSMiddleware, SessionMiddleware (signed cookie, HttpOnly, "readable but not modifiable"), HTTPSRedirectMiddleware, TrustedHostMiddleware (Host-header attacks), RequestBodyLimitMiddleware, GZipMiddleware.

## 3. API-key infrastructure landscape

- Key form (random): secrets module — token_bytes/token_hex/token_urlsafe over OS randomness; DEFAULT_ENTROPY; "32 bytes (256 bits) of randomness is sufficient" (2015 belief); prefer secrets over random (docs.python.org/3/library/secrets.html).
- Key form (structured): JWT — RFC 7519 registered claims iss/sub/aud/exp/nbf/iat/jti; aud: each intended recipient "MUST identify itself with a value in the audience claim" or reject; jti "can be used to prevent the JWT from being replayed"; jwt.io: signed ≠ secret — payload readable by anyone.
- Hashed-at-rest + storage: OWASP Key Management (cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Key_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html) — API keys never committed to repos, never stored plaintext, dedicated vault/HSM, all operations in the vault; env-var loading (FastMCP configuration) vs config-constant SECRET_KEY (FastAPI tutorial) are the two env/file forms seen.
- Rotation/revocation: cryptoperiods limit the window of exposure; originator vs recipient usage periods give a dual-key overlap (encrypt ≤2y; decrypt ≤3y beyond); JWKS rotation without server changes (FastMCP); revoke on usage-agreement violation (OWASP REST); jti+aud denylist until exp (OWASP REST JWT).
- Verification: hmac.compare_digest — designed "to prevent timing analysis by avoiding content-based short circuiting behaviour" (docs.python.org/3/library/hmac.html); OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet: hash comparisons must return in constant time; hash-lookup form: store keys hashed, look up by digest (ecosystem practice, e.g. blog.masteringbackend.com FastAPI auth).

## 4. Threat-model literature

- STRIDE (Microsoft; Kohnfelder & Garg 1999): Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege — six classes, each mapped to a violated property (authentication, integrity, non-repudiation, confidentiality, availability, authorization).
- RBAC (NIST): formalized 1992 by Ferraiolo/Kuhn; ANSI/INCITS 359-2004, revised INCITS 359-2012; users→roles→privileges (csrc.nist.gov/projects/role-based-access-control). ABAC (NIST SP 800-162): authorization by evaluating subject/object/operation/environment attributes against policy; contrast: RBAC "does not easily support multi-factor decisions".
- Bearer-token threats: RFC 6750 §5.1 names token manufacture/modification, token disclosure, token redirect (one resource server's token replayed at another), token replay; mitigations: audience restriction in the token, TLS, short-lived (≤1h), scoped. RFC 6819 (OAuth 2.0 threat model): eavesdropping on transport, replay, guessing, leakage via logs/referrers. RFC 8725 (JWT BCP): alg "none", RS256→HS256 confusion (downgrade), weak symmetric keys, substitution/cross-JWT confusion; mitigations: validate iss/sub, use aud, explicit typing. OWASP OAuth2 Cheat Sheet: bearer tokens "should be audience-restricted, preferably to a single Resource Server".
- Corroboration: NIST IR 8587 (2026): "all tokens and assertions MUST include explicit audience fields, and all access control mechanisms MUST reject tokens with incorrect or missing audience restrictions."

## 1. THE CLAIMS' VERDICTS (the claims lane: extract → research → verify → rule)

**CONFIRMED — OunceMCP's verified-token model (SEC-1..12).** Verified at its own docs (concepts/security/, guides/safe-writes/) and cross-checked against the 2026-11-22 census (.plans/ideation/2026-11-22-prioritree-mcp/reports/census/ouncemcp.md): CONSISTENT — handles/approval (pt 3), signed cursors + redacted traces (pts 2/5), the FastMCP 4.1.6 substrate (pt 4); NO contradictions. **CONFIRMED — the FastAPI/FastMCP/Starlette forms, at their docs.** FastAPI: APIKeyHeader/APIKeyQuery/APIKeyCookie, OAuth2PasswordBearer (the Bearer token as str, 401 on missing), the OpenAPI scheme integration, the JWT tutorial's HS256 + sub/exp + dummy-hash timing equalization. **CONFIRMED — the threat-model literature's classes.** STRIDE's six classes (Kohnfelder & Garg 1999), each mapped to its violated property (authentication, integrity, non-repudiation, confidentiality, availability, authorization); RFC 6750 §5.1's bearer threats (token manufacture/modification/disclosure/redirect/replay) with the mitigations (audience restriction, TLS, short-lived ≤1h, scoped); RFC 6819's eavesdropping/replay/guessing/leakage-via-logs; RFC 8725's JWT downgrades (alg "none", RS256→HS256 confusion, weak symmetric keys, cross-JWT confusion); NIST's RBAC (Ferraiolo/Kuhn 1992, INCITS 359-2012; users→roles→privileges) and ABAC (SP 800-162; RBAC "does not easily support multi-factor decisions"); NIST IR 8587 (2026): all tokens MUST carry explicit audience, all access control MUST reject wrong/missing audience.

(ii) Hashed-at-rest COSTS MORE BYTES than the token it guards (SHA-256 digest = 64 hex chars vs the 22-char 128-bit token; "the purchase is the plaintext's absence, not size") — priced and accepted per OWASP's never-plaintext.

**PRICED-AND-REFUSED — one claim confirmed at its source, refused at this tree's scale.** OWASP's vault/HSM custody ("dedicated vault/HSM, all operations in the vault"): confirmed as the enterprise form; priced by keisan at $28.80/yr (AWS Secrets Manager) / $4.32/yr (GCP) + per-call fees + the cloud-credential chain (the runner needs cloud credentials to fetch the key — "a second credential problem bigger than the first") — refused at the ≤8-operator scale under the free-tier spirit (§2c).

## 2. THE CANDIDATE MAP (every candidate named with its source and its class)

**(a) THE LEADING SHAPE — the random-token API key + the file store + hashed-at-rest + the per-route dependency + the RBAC grant map.** The bench's findings support it on every axis measured:

The env-var form banked alongside ($0, the .envrc precedent).

**(b) THE JWT FORM — priced and unneeded at this scale.** 110-200 B minimum, 200-800 B typical = 9.1×-36.4× the 22-B token on the wire; RS256's signature alone 342 B + ~1.7 KB private-PEM custody — a SECOND secret to store, rotate, and never commit (the signing-key problem the API key does not have); the machinery priced: expiry/claims/kid/rotation/jti + the downgrade class (RFC 8725: alg "none", RS→HS confusion, weak symmetric keys) + the audience discipline (NIST IR 8587) — all against the ≤8-operator scale where a one-line file already meets the need: "infrastructure without a need." Verification cost is NOT the issue (10-500 µs, still noise) — the machinery is. Banked as the scale fence's far side (§5).

**(c) THE SECRET-MANAGER FORM — priced and refused.** AWS $2.40/mo = $28.80/yr; GCP $0.36/mo = $4.32/yr — plus per-call fees and the credential-chain exposure: the runner needs cloud credentials to fetch the key, a second credential problem bigger than the first. **(d) THE OAUTH/FULL-PROVIDER FORM — priced against the llm-class constraint and the local scale.** FastMCP's provider spectrum (OAuthProvider = a full authorization server; OAuthProxy = GitHub/Google/Azure/AWS; RemoteAuthProvider = DCR; MultiAuth = first-wins): each names an external identity authority and a browser consent ceremony; the llm comparator CANNOT ride a human's OAuth consent without violating the no-human-approval-gate constraint — the llm needs its own credential, which is the API key again. The local file's $0 wins at every axis measured. Banked for the multi-tenant future (§5).

**(e) THE BENCH-SURFACED MCP-TIER CANDIDATE — OunceMCP's verified-token + policies** (the widening ruling's named form): identity from the verified token (SEC-1), hide-and-refuse per identity (SEC-2/3), audience/passthrough guards (SEC-4), composing at the OunceServer construction (mcp_server.py:113); its scope honestly named: the auth applies to FastMCP's HTTP-based transports only — the --serve form at :8100 is inside the scope; stdio is not (the §4 divergence).

**RESIDUALS (a) LEAVES OPEN — named for the evaluation:**

- (i) THE SPAWN-AS-CREDENTIAL (the local-user trust): stdio runs as the spawning user; OunceMCP's own default stdio_policy="trust" (every tool visible/callable; FastMCP skips component authorization over stdio; `ouncemcp check` warns stdio-skips-policy); the llm comparator rides the harness's stdio spawn — trusted as the local user.
